related_questions.question: What are the GI symptoms of Covid-19?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can cause a range of gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. These symptoms can be the initial sign of infection or develop later, and may even persist as part of long COVID, according to the University of Nebraska Medical Center. Some individuals may experience GI symptoms as their only indication of COVID-19, according to the University of Nebraska Medical Center. The virus can affect the gut because the receptors it uses to enter cells are also present in the digestive system.

text_blocks.snippet: GI symptoms can occur in up to 50% of COVID-19 patients. They may appear early in the course of the infection, or they may develop later. GI symptoms can also be a sign of long COVID, which is the ongoing symptoms that some people experience after recovering from COVID-19.

It is important to note that GI symptoms can also be caused by other conditions, such as food poisoning or gastroenteritis. If you experience GI symptoms, it is recommended to seek medical attention to determine the underlying cause.
